subject.title: [Bug] Sandbox validateEnvVarValue base64 heuristic false-positives on legitimate long alphanumeric values

question: Should OpenClaw narrow the sandbox env credential-data warning to structured base64 values on credential-looking env names?
rationale: The false positive is source-reproducible, but the fix changes advisory sandbox credential-warning coverage, so automation should not choose that security-boundary tradeoff.

options.title: Approve narrow warning policy
options.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main and land the key-aware structured-base64 sanitizer if sandbox/security owners accept fewer neutral-name warnings.

options.title: Preserve broader warning coverage
options.body: Keep the issue open and request a different heuristic that reduces false positives without requiring credential-like names.

options.title: Treat broad warnings as intentional
options.body: Close only after maintainers decide the conservative warning policy is preferred and document that behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow warning policy
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main and land the key-aware structured-base64 sanitizer if sandbox/security owners accept fewer neutral-name warnings.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sanitizer and adjacent warning tests, making them the strongest history-backed owner for this policy choice.
